  • Returns: number, the new image's 0-based id, or -1 if the texture id is unknown.
  • Notes: unlike a panel, an image is created without a Mask; add one with ShroudSetMask when you want it to clip its children.
local tex = ShroudLoadTexture("icon.png")
local img = ShroudUIImage(10, 10, 64, 64, tex)
ShroudConsoleLog("image id = " .. img)

ShroudUIText¶

ShroudUIText(text: string, fontSize: number, x: number, y: number, width: number, height: number, parentID: number, parentKind: UI, depth: number) -> number

  • text: string, the initial label string.
  • fontSize: number, point size for the label.
  • x, y: number, top-left offset from the canvas top-left; y negated internally.
  • width, height: number, size of the text rect in pixels.
  • parentID: number, parent widget id, or -1 for the canvas. Optional, defaults -1.
  • parentKind: UI, parent kind (UI.Image, UI.Text, UI.Panel, UI.Button, else canvas). Optional, defaults UI.None.
  • depth: number, accepted but not applied. Optional, defaults -1.
  • Returns: number, the new label's 0-based id. This call has no texture dependency and does not return -1.
local label = ShroudUIText("Hello, Avatar", 18, 20, 20, 200, 30)
ShroudModifyText(label, "Gold: " .. ShroudPlayerGold)

ShroudUIButton¶

ShroudUIButton(x: number, y: number, width: number, height: number, textureID: number, parentID: number, parentKind: UI, depth: number) -> number

  • x, y: number, top-left offset from the canvas top-left; y negated internally.
  • width, height: number, size in pixels.
  • textureID: number, the button face texture id. Although it defaults to -1, a button requires a valid texture — an unknown id makes the call fail.
  • parentID: number, parent widget id, or -1 for the canvas. Optional, defaults -1.
  • parentKind: UI, parent kind (UI.Image, UI.Text, UI.Panel, UI.Button, else canvas). Optional, defaults UI.None.
  • depth: number, accepted but not applied. Optional, defaults -1.
  • Returns: number, the new button's 0-based id, or -1 if the texture id is unknown.
  • Notes: the button wires click and enter/exit listeners; handle clicks through ShroudSetClickListener and the ShroudOnMouseClick callback.
local face = ShroudLoadTexture("button.png")
local btn = ShroudUIButton(50, 100, 120, 32, face)
if btn ~= -1 then ShroudSetClickListener(btn, UI.Button) end

ShroudUIInput¶

ShroudUIInput(x: number, y: number, width: number, height: number, parentID: number, parentKind: UI) -> number

  • x, y: number, top-left offset from the canvas top-left; y negated internally.
  • width, height: number, size in pixels. Optional, both default 20.
  • parentID: number, parent widget id, or -1 for the canvas. Optional, defaults -1.
  • parentKind: UI, parent kind — an input may parent only under UI.Image or UI.Panel (anything else falls back to the canvas). Optional, defaults UI.None.
  • Returns: number, the new input's 0-based id. No texture dependency; does not return -1.
  • Notes: starts with an italic "Enter text..." placeholder; read the field with ShroudGetInputText and set it with ShroudSetInputText.
local box = ShroudUIInput(20, 200, 180, 24)
ShroudSetPlaceholderText(box, "search...")
ShroudConsoleLog("typed: " .. (ShroudGetInputText(box) or ""))

ShroudUIToggle¶

ShroudUIToggle(x: number, y: number, width: number, height: number, parentID: number, parentKind: UI) -> number

  • x, y: number, top-left offset from the canvas top-left; y negated internally.
  • width, height: number, size in pixels. Optional, both default 20.
  • parentID: number, parent widget id, or -1 for the canvas. Optional, defaults -1.
  • parentKind: UI, parent kind — a toggle may parent only under UI.Image or UI.Panel (anything else falls back to the canvas). Optional, defaults UI.None.
  • Returns: number, the new toggle's 0-based id. No texture dependency; does not return -1.
  • Notes: read/write the checked state with ShroudGetToggle/ShroudSetToggle; state changes fire the ShroudOnToggleChange callback.
local chk = ShroudUIToggle(20, 240, 20, 20)
ShroudSetToggle(chk, true)

ShroudSetPosition¶

ShroudSetPosition(id: number, kind: UI, x: number, y: number) -> boolean

  • id: number, the widget id.
  • kind: UI, its kind. Accepts UI.Image, UI.Text, UI.Panel, UI.Button, UI.Toggle, UI.Input.
  • x, y: number, new top-left offset from the canvas top-left. Optional, both default 0. y is negated internally, so positive y moves the widget down.
  • Returns: boolean, true on success; false if kind is UI.None, id is negative, or id is out of range for that kind.
ShroudSetPosition(panel, UI.Panel, 100, 150)

ShroudGetPosition¶

ShroudGetPosition(id: number, kind: UI) -> LuaVector2

  • id: number, the widget id.
  • kind: UI, its kind. Accepts UI.Image, UI.Text, UI.Panel, UI.Button, UI.Toggle, UI.Input.
  • Returns: a LuaVector2 userdata object with numeric fields x and y (accessed as pos.x / pos.y), or nil if kind is UI.None, id is negative, or id is out of range. This is a registered userdata, not a Lua table, so type(pos) is "userdata". The returned y is un-negated, so it matches the value you gave ShroudSetPosition.
local pos = ShroudGetPosition(panel, UI.Panel)
if pos then
    ShroudConsoleLog("panel at " .. pos.x .. ", " .. pos.y)
end

ShroudSetSize¶

ShroudSetSize(id: number, kind: UI, width: number, height: number) -> boolean

  • id: number, the widget id.
  • kind: UI, its kind. Applies to UI.Image, UI.Text, UI.Panel, UI.Button only — UI.Toggle and UI.Input are not handled and return false.
  • width, height: number, the new size in pixels. Optional, both default 0.
  • Returns: boolean, true on success; false for an unsupported kind, UI.None, a negative id, or an out-of-range id.
ShroudSetSize(panel, UI.Panel, 320, 240)

ShroudSetScale¶

ShroudSetScale(id: number, kind: UI, scale: number) -> boolean

  • id: number, the widget id.
  • kind: UI, its kind. Applies to UI.Image, UI.Text, UI.Panel, UI.Button.
  • scale: number, a single uniform factor applied to both the x and y local scale. Optional, defaults 1.
  • Returns: boolean, true on success; false for an unsupported kind, UI.None, a negative id, or an out-of-range id.
ShroudSetScale(img, UI.Image, 1.5)

ShroudSetPivot¶

ShroudSetPivot(id: number, kind: UI, x: number, y: number) -> boolean

  • id: number, the widget id.
  • kind: UI, its kind. Applies to UI.Image, UI.Text, UI.Panel, UI.Button.
  • x, y: number, the pivot in 0..1 rect space (0,0 is bottom-left, 1,1 top-right). Optional, both default 0.
  • Returns: boolean, true on success; false for an unsupported kind, UI.None, a negative id, or an out-of-range id.
  • Notes: as a side effect this also multiplies the widget's current anchored position by the new pivot x and y, so setting the pivot generally shifts the widget — set the pivot before positioning, then call ShroudSetPosition.
ShroudSetPivot(img, UI.Image, 0.5, 0.5)
ShroudSetPosition(img, UI.Image, 100, 100)

ShroudSetAnchorMin¶

ShroudSetAnchorMin(id: number, kind: UI, x: number, y: number) -> boolean

  • id: number, the widget id.
  • kind: UI, its kind. Applies to UI.Image, UI.Text, UI.Panel, UI.Button.
  • x, y: number, the minimum anchor in 0..1 of the parent rect. Optional, both default 0.
  • Returns: boolean, true on success; false for an unsupported kind, UI.None, a negative id, or an out-of-range id.
ShroudSetAnchorMin(panel, UI.Panel, 0, 0)
ShroudSetAnchorMax(panel, UI.Panel, 1, 1)

ShroudSetAnchorMax¶

ShroudSetAnchorMax(id: number, kind: UI, x: number, y: number) -> boolean Same as ShroudSetAnchorMin but sets the maximum anchor corner. Applies to UI.Image, UI.Text, UI.Panel, UI.Button; x, y default 0; returns false for an unsupported kind, UI.None, a negative id, or an out-of-range id.

ShroudRotateObject¶

ShroudRotateObject(id: number, kind: UI, degrees: number) -> boolean

  • id: number, the widget id.
  • kind: UI, its kind. Applies to UI.Image, UI.Text, UI.Panel, UI.Button.
  • degrees: number, the absolute Z rotation in degrees. Optional, defaults 0. This sets, not accumulates — the value replaces the current rotation.
  • Returns: boolean, true on success; false for an unsupported kind, UI.None, a negative id, or an out-of-range id.
ShroudRotateObject(img, UI.Image, 45)

ShroudSetColor¶

ShroudSetColor(id: number, kind: UI, hexColor: string) -> boolean

  • id: number, the widget id.
  • kind: UI, its kind. Applies to UI.Image, UI.Text, UI.Panel, UI.Toggle, UI.Input. UI.Button is rejected — tint a button with ShroudSetButtonColor.
  • hexColor: string, an HTML color string. Always include the leading # ("#RRGGBB" or "#RRGGBBAA"). The parse happens before any # fix-up, so a string without a leading # does not parse — it yields transparent black rather than being auto-corrected.
  • Returns: boolean, true on success; false if kind is UI.None or UI.Button, id is negative, or id is out of range.
  • Notes: an unparseable hex string does not fail the call — it resolves to transparent black and still returns true, so validate your color strings (and keep the #).
ShroudSetColor(panel, UI.Panel, "#204060")
ShroudSetColor(label, UI.Text, "#FFCC00")

ShroudSetTransparency¶

ShroudSetTransparency(id: number, kind: UI, alpha: number) -> boolean

  • id: number, the widget id.
  • kind: UI, its kind. Applies to UI.Image, UI.Button, UI.Panel, UI.Text, UI.Toggle, UI.Input.
  • alpha: number, the alpha channel, 0 fully transparent to 1 fully opaque.
  • Returns: boolean, true on success; false if kind is UI.None, id is negative, or id is out of range.
ShroudSetTransparency(panel, UI.Panel, 0.75)

ShroudModifyImage¶

ShroudModifyImage(id: number, kind: UI, textureID: number) -> boolean

  • id: number, the widget id.
  • kind: UI, its kind. Applies to UI.Image, UI.Panel, UI.Button, UI.Input. UI.Text is rejected.
  • textureID: number, the new texture id from ShroudLoadTexture.
  • Returns: boolean, true on success; false if kind is UI.Text, id is negative, the texture id is unknown, or id is out of range for that kind.
local hover = ShroudLoadTexture("panel_hover.png")
ShroudModifyImage(panel, UI.Panel, hover)

ShroudModifyText¶

ShroudModifyText(id: number, text: string) -> boolean

  • id: number, a text-widget id (from ShroudUIText). There is no kind parameter — this always targets a text label.
  • text: string, the replacement string. Optional, defaults "".
  • Returns: boolean, true on success; false if id is negative or out of range for the text list.
ShroudModifyText(label, "HP: " .. ShroudPlayerCurrentHealth)

ShroudSetTextAlignment¶

ShroudSetTextAlignment(id: number, anchor: TextAnchor) -> boolean

  • id: number, a text-widget id (from ShroudUIText). No kind parameter.
  • anchor: TextAnchor, one of UpperLeft, UpperCenter, UpperRight, MiddleLeft, MiddleCenter, MiddleRight, LowerLeft, LowerCenter, LowerRight. Optional, defaults UpperLeft.
  • Returns: boolean, true on success; false only when id is negative.
  • Notes: this guards against a negative id but does not bounds-check the upper end — passing an id at or beyond the text-widget count throws. Only pass ids returned by ShroudUIText.
ShroudSetTextAlignment(label, TextAnchor.MiddleCenter)

ShroudSetFontSize¶

ShroudSetFontSize(id: number, kind: UI, size: number) -> boolean

  • id: number, the widget id.
  • kind: UI, its kind. Applies to UI.Text and UI.Input only; for an input it sizes both the text and the placeholder.
  • size: number, the new font point size.
  • Returns: boolean, true on success; false for any other kind, a negative id, or an out-of-range id.
ShroudSetFontSize(label, UI.Text, 24)

ShroudSetMask¶

ShroudSetMask(id: number, kind: UI) -> boolean

  • id: number, the widget id.
  • kind: UI, its kind. Applies to UI.Image and UI.Panel only.
  • Returns: boolean, true if a Mask was added; false if the kind is unsupported, id is negative or out of range, or the widget already has a Mask.
  • Notes: adds a Unity Mask component so child widgets are clipped to this widget's rect. Use it to build scroll regions or clipped panels. A panel already ships with a Mask, so ShroudSetMask(panel, UI.Panel) returns false and changes nothing — panels clip their children out of the box. This call is meant for an image, which is created without a Mask; it only re-adds a Mask to a panel after one was removed with ShroudUnsetMask.
-- An image has no Mask by default, so this adds one and returns true:
ShroudSetMask(img, UI.Image)

ShroudUnsetMask¶

ShroudUnsetMask(id: number, kind: UI) -> boolean

  • id: number, the widget id.
  • kind: UI, its kind. Applies to UI.Image and UI.Panel only.
  • Returns: boolean, true if a Mask was removed; false if the kind is unsupported, id is negative or out of range, or the widget has no Mask to remove.
  • Notes: because a panel is created with a Mask, ShroudUnsetMask(panel, UI.Panel) succeeds and stops the panel from clipping its children.
-- Remove a panel's default Mask so its children can overflow its rect:
ShroudUnsetMask(panel, UI.Panel)

UI widgets: parenting, visibility, and behavior¶

These functions restructure and control retained-mode widgets created by the ShroudUI* family (see the widget-creation section). Every widget is addressed by the 0-based id its create call returned plus its UI kind (UI.Panel, UI.Image, UI.Text, UI.Button, UI.Toggle, UI.Input; UI.None is the invalid/unset value). All of them fail soft: an out-of-range id, UI.None, or an unsupported kind returns the failure value rather than throwing. Two frozen quirks run through this group: the parenting setters (ShroudSetParent and the four typed variants) return -1 even when they succeed, and the Dragguable spelling is permanent. Like the rest of the retained-widget API these are only valid once widgets exist, so call them from a callback (ShroudOnStart, ShroudOnUpdate, and so on), not at file scope.

Function Call What it does
ShroudSetParent ShroudSetParent(id, kind, parentId, parentKind) Reparent any widget under any widget
ShroudSetPanelParent ShroudSetPanelParent(panelId, parentId, parentKind) Reparent a panel; -1 detaches to canvas
ShroudSetImageParent ShroudSetImageParent(imageId, parentId, parentKind) Reparent an image; -1 detaches to canvas
ShroudSetTextParent ShroudSetTextParent(textId, parentId, parentKind) Reparent a text; -1 detaches to canvas
ShroudSetButtonParent ShroudSetButtonParent(buttonId, parentId, parentKind) Reparent a button; -1 detaches to canvas
ShroudGetParentID ShroudGetParentID(id, kind) Id of the widget's parent widget
ShroudGetParentObjectKind ShroudGetParentObjectKind(id, kind) UI kind of the widget's parent
ShroudSetDragguable ShroudSetDragguable(id, kind) Make a panel/image draggable
ShroudUnsetDragguable ShroudUnsetDragguable(id, kind) Remove draggability
ShroudSetResizable ShroudSetResizable(id, kind, direction) Let a draggable panel be resized
ShroudMinMaxSize ShroudMinMaxSize(id, kind, min, max, direction) Clamp resize range of a draggable panel/image
ShroudSetInOutListener ShroudSetInOutListener(id, kind) Fire mouse over/out callbacks for a widget
ShroudUnsetInOutListener ShroudUnsetInOutListener(id, kind) Remove the over/out listener
ShroudSetClickListener ShroudSetClickListener(id, kind) Fire the mouse-click callback for a widget
ShroudUnsetClickListener ShroudUnsetClickListener(id, kind) Remove the click listener
ShroudRaycastObject ShroudRaycastObject(id, kind, enable) Toggle whether a widget catches the pointer
ShroudHideObject ShroudHideObject(id, kind) Deactivate one widget
ShroudShowObject ShroudShowObject(id, kind) Reactivate one widget
ShroudHideLuaUI ShroudHideLuaUI() Hide the whole addon canvas
ShroudShowLuaUI ShroudShowLuaUI() Show the whole addon canvas
ShroudDestroyObject ShroudDestroyObject(id, kind) Destroy a widget and free its slot

ShroudSetParent¶

ShroudSetParent(id: number, kind: UI, parentId: number, parentKind: UI) -> number

  • id: number, 0-based id of the child widget.
  • kind: UI, the child widget's kind. Any of the six kinds may be a child.
  • parentId: number, 0-based id of the parent widget.
  • parentKind: UI, the parent widget's kind. Only UI.Image, UI.Text, UI.Panel, and UI.Button are valid parents; a UI.Toggle or UI.Input child rejects UI.Button/UI.Text parents.
  • Returns: number. Always -1, even on success (frozen quirk) — do not treat the return as an error code. id < 0 or parentId < 0 returns -1 with no change.
  • Notes: reparents keeping local layout (world-position-stays is false), so the child's size and anchored position are preserved relative to the new parent. Reparenting a panel under a panel removes the child's bring-to-front behavior.
function ShroudOnStart()
    parent = ShroudUIPanel(100, 100, 200, 200)
    child  = ShroudUIText("nested", 24, 10, 10, 120, 30)
    ShroudSetParent(child, UI.Text, parent, UI.Panel)
    -- return is always -1; confirm with GetParentID instead
    ShroudConsoleLog("child parent id = " .. ShroudGetParentID(child, UI.Text))
end

ShroudSetPanelParent¶

ShroudSetPanelParent(panelId: number, parentId: number, parentKind: UI) -> number Reparent a panel, with the child kind fixed to UI.Panel.

  • panelId: number, 0-based id of the panel to reparent.
  • parentId: number, 0-based id of the parent widget, or -1 to detach to the top-level addon canvas.
  • parentKind: UI, the parent widget's kind (UI.Image/UI.Text/UI.Panel/UI.Button).
  • Returns: number. Always -1 (frozen quirk).
  • Notes: parentId = -1 reparents the panel to the root canvas and restores its bring-to-front component, which is the way to promote a nested panel back to a free-floating window.
function ShroudOnStart()
    win = ShroudUIPanel(200, 200, 300, 200)
    ShroudSetPanelParent(win, -1, UI.Panel)   -- float at canvas top level
    ShroudSetDragguable(win, UI.Panel)
end

ShroudSetImageParent¶

ShroudSetImageParent(imageId: number, parentId: number, parentKind: UI) -> number Reparent an image, with the child kind fixed to UI.Image. Same as ShroudSetPanelParent but for an image widget; parentId = -1 detaches to the canvas. Returns -1 even on success.

icon = ShroudSetImageParent(icon, panel, UI.Panel)  -- ignore the return; it is -1

ShroudSetTextParent¶

ShroudSetTextParent(textId: number, parentId: number, parentKind: UI) -> number Reparent a text widget, with the child kind fixed to UI.Text. Same as ShroudSetPanelParent but for a text widget; parentId = -1 detaches to the canvas. Returns -1 even on success.

ShroudSetTextParent(label, panel, UI.Panel)

ShroudSetButtonParent¶

ShroudSetButtonParent(buttonId: number, parentId: number, parentKind: UI) -> number Reparent a button, with the child kind fixed to UI.Button. Same as ShroudSetPanelParent but for a button widget; parentId = -1 detaches to the canvas. Returns -1 even on success.

ShroudSetButtonParent(okButton, panel, UI.Panel)

ShroudGetParentID¶

ShroudGetParentID(id: number, kind: UI) -> number

  • id: number, 0-based id of the widget whose parent you want.
  • kind: UI, the widget's own kind.
  • Returns: number. The 0-based id of the parent widget, or -1 when the widget is invalid, kind is UI.None, or its parent is the root canvas rather than another addon widget.
  • Notes: the returned id is only meaningful together with ShroudGetParentObjectKind — the id indexes whichever widget list the parent belongs to, so read both to identify the parent unambiguously.
pid = ShroudGetParentID(child, UI.Text)
if pid >= 0 then
    ShroudConsoleLog("parent id " .. pid .. " kind " .. ShroudGetParentObjectKind(child, UI.Text))
end

ShroudGetParentObjectKind¶

ShroudGetParentObjectKind(id: number, kind: UI) -> UI

  • id: number, 0-based id of the widget.
  • kind: UI, the widget's own kind.
  • Returns: UI. The parent widget's kind, or UI.None when the widget is invalid, kind is UI.None, or the parent is the root canvas.
  • Notes: pair with ShroudGetParentID to fully resolve the parent.
kind = ShroudGetParentObjectKind(child, UI.Text)
if kind == UI.Panel then ShroudConsoleLog("child sits inside a panel") end

ShroudSetDragguable¶

ShroudSetDragguable(id: number, kind: UI) -> boolean

  • id: number, 0-based id of the widget.
  • kind: UI, must be UI.Panel or UI.Image; other kinds are ignored.
  • Returns: boolean. true when drag support was added, false for an unsupported kind, an invalid id, or a widget that is already draggable.
  • Notes: the spelling Dragguable is frozen; do not correct it. Adds pointer-drag and bring-to-front behavior. Required before ShroudSetResizable or ShroudMinMaxSize will take effect.
function ShroudOnStart()
    win = ShroudUIPanel(300, 300, 260, 180)
    if ShroudSetDragguable(win, UI.Panel) then
        ShroudConsoleLog("panel is now draggable")
    end
end

ShroudUnsetDragguable¶

ShroudUnsetDragguable(id: number, kind: UI) -> boolean Remove drag/bring-to-front support. Same as ShroudSetDragguable but in reverse: kind must be UI.Panel or UI.Image. Returns true when a drag component was present and removed, false when the widget was not draggable or the kind is unsupported.

ShroudUnsetDragguable(win, UI.Panel)

ShroudSetResizable¶

ShroudSetResizable(id: number, kind: UI, direction: string) -> boolean

  • id: number, 0-based id of the panel.
  • kind: UI, only UI.Panel is supported.
  • direction: string, case-insensitive: "horizontal", "vertical", "corner" (both axes), or "none" (disables resizing).
  • Returns: boolean. true when applied, false for a non-panel, an invalid id, or a panel that is not already draggable.
  • Notes: the panel must first be made draggable with ShroudSetDragguable; without the drag component this is a no-op that returns false.
ShroudSetDragguable(win, UI.Panel)
ShroudSetResizable(win, UI.Panel, "corner")

ShroudMinMaxSize¶

ShroudMinMaxSize(id: number, kind: UI, min: number, max: number, direction: string) -> boolean

  • id: number, 0-based id of the widget.
  • kind: UI, only UI.Panel or UI.Image are supported.
  • min: number, minimum size in pixels for the chosen axis/axes.
  • max: number, maximum size in pixels.
  • direction: string, case-insensitive: "horizontal", "vertical", "corner" (both axes), or "none" (resets the clamp to 20–1000 on both axes).
  • Returns: boolean. true when applied, false for an unsupported kind, an invalid id, or a widget that is not already draggable.
  • Notes: like ShroudSetResizable, the widget must already be draggable (ShroudSetDragguable) for the clamp to attach.
ShroudSetDragguable(win, UI.Panel)
ShroudSetResizable(win, UI.Panel, "corner")
ShroudMinMaxSize(win, UI.Panel, 120, 600, "corner")

ShroudSetInOutListener¶

ShroudSetInOutListener(id: number, kind: UI) -> boolean

  • id: number, 0-based id of the widget.
  • kind: UI, supported for UI.Image, UI.Panel, UI.Text, and UI.Button.
  • Returns: boolean. true when the listener was added, false for an unsupported kind (UI.Toggle/UI.Input), an invalid id, or a widget that already has one.
  • Notes: while the listener is attached, moving the pointer onto the widget invokes your ShroudOnMouseOver(id, kind) callback and moving off invokes ShroudOnMouseOut(id, kind).
function ShroudOnStart()
    box = ShroudUIPanel(100, 100, 150, 80)
    ShroudSetInOutListener(box, UI.Panel)
end
function ShroudOnMouseOver(id, kind)
    ShroudConsoleLog("hovering widget " .. id)
end

ShroudUnsetInOutListener¶

ShroudUnsetInOutListener(id: number, kind: UI) -> boolean Remove the over/out listener. Same kinds as ShroudSetInOutListener (UI.Image/UI.Panel/UI.Text/UI.Button).

  • Returns: boolean. false for UI.None/invalid id.
  • Notes: frozen quirk — the removal branch tests for the drag component, not the listener, so it only strips the listener from widgets that are not also draggable and returns false on a draggable widget. To be certain a widget stops firing over/out, destroy and recreate it rather than relying on this call for a draggable one.
ShroudUnsetInOutListener(box, UI.Panel)

ShroudSetClickListener¶

ShroudSetClickListener(id: number, kind: UI) -> boolean

  • id: number, 0-based id of the widget.
  • kind: UI, supported for UI.Image, UI.Panel, UI.Text, and UI.Button.
  • Returns: boolean. true when the listener was added, false for an unsupported kind (UI.Toggle/UI.Input), an invalid id, or a widget that already has one.
  • Notes: while attached, releasing the pointer over the widget invokes your ShroudOnMouseClick(id, kind) callback. Useful for making a plain image or panel act like a button.
function ShroudOnStart()
    tile = ShroudUIImage(100, 100, 64, 64, ShroudLoadTexture("tile.png"))
    ShroudSetClickListener(tile, UI.Image)
end
function ShroudOnMouseClick(id, kind)
    ShroudConsoleLog("clicked widget " .. id)
end

ShroudUnsetClickListener¶

ShroudUnsetClickListener(id: number, kind: UI) -> boolean Remove the click listener. Accepts only UI.Image and UI.Panel (UI.Text and UI.Button are rejected up front and return false).

  • Returns: boolean. false for UI.None, an invalid id, or a UI.Text/UI.Button kind.
  • Notes: frozen quirk — the removal branch is inverted (it destroys only when no listener is present), so it does not actually strip a live click listener. To reliably stop click handling, destroy the widget with ShroudDestroyObject and recreate it.
ShroudUnsetClickListener(tile, UI.Image)

ShroudRaycastObject¶

ShroudRaycastObject(id: number, kind: UI, enable: boolean) -> boolean

  • id: number, 0-based id of the widget.
  • kind: UI, any of the six widget kinds.
  • enable: boolean, true to make the widget catch the pointer, false to let clicks and hovers pass through to whatever is behind it.
  • Returns: boolean. true when applied, false for UI.None or an out-of-range id.
  • Notes: toggles the underlying graphic's raycast target. Disable it on a decorative overlay so it does not block the widgets beneath it.
overlay = ShroudUIImage(0, 0, 400, 400, ShroudLoadTexture("overlay.png"))
ShroudRaycastObject(overlay, UI.Image, false)  -- clicks fall through

ShroudHideObject¶

ShroudHideObject(id: number, kind: UI) -> boolean

  • id: number, 0-based id of the widget.
  • kind: UI, supported only for UI.Image, UI.Text, UI.Panel, and UI.Button. A UI.Toggle or UI.Input widget is not handled and cannot be hidden with this call — it returns false and does nothing.
  • Returns: boolean. true when the widget was deactivated, false for UI.None, an out-of-range id, or an unsupported kind (UI.Toggle/UI.Input).
  • Notes: deactivates the widget's GameObject; its children hide with it, and its id and state are retained for a later ShroudShowObject. To hide a toggle or input, parent it under a panel and hide the panel instead.
if ShroudGetToggle(myToggle) == false then
    ShroudHideObject(panel, UI.Panel)
end

ShroudShowObject¶

ShroudShowObject(id: number, kind: UI) -> boolean Reactivate a widget previously hidden with ShroudHideObject. Same as ShroudHideObject but sets the widget active again; supported only for UI.Image, UI.Text, UI.Panel, and UI.Button. A UI.Toggle or UI.Input widget cannot be reactivated with this call — it returns false and does nothing. Returns false for UI.None, an invalid id, or an unsupported kind.

ShroudShowObject(panel, UI.Panel)

ShroudHideLuaUI¶

ShroudHideLuaUI() -> boolean

  • Returns: boolean. true when the addon canvas was hidden, false if no canvas exists yet.
  • Notes: deactivates the entire addon canvas at once, hiding every widget your addon created without destroying them. Pair with ShroudShowLuaUI. Use it for a global show/hide hotkey.
function ShroudOnUpdate()
    if ShroudGetOnKeyDown("f8") then
        ShroudHideLuaUI()
    end
end

ShroudShowLuaUI¶

ShroudShowLuaUI() -> boolean Reactivate the whole addon canvas. Same as ShroudHideLuaUI but reveals every widget again; returns true when the canvas exists, false otherwise.

ShroudShowLuaUI()

ShroudDestroyObject¶

ShroudDestroyObject(id: number, kind: UI) -> boolean

  • id: number, 0-based id of the widget to destroy.
  • kind: UI, any of the six widget kinds.
  • Returns: boolean. true when the widget was destroyed, false for UI.None or an out-of-range id.
  • Notes: destroys the GameObject and nulls its slot in the widget list. The id is not renumbered — the freed slot is reused by the next widget you create of that kind, so a create call after a destroy can hand back the same id. Do not keep using an id after destroying it.
ShroudDestroyObject(panel, UI.Panel)
panel = nil

UI widgets: buttons, inputs, and toggles¶

These functions style and read the interactive widgets created by ShroudUIButton, ShroudUIInput, and ShroudUIToggle. Every call takes the 0-based integer id that the matching create call returned. The input and button-color/button-image functions guard the id with an explicit >= 0 check, so an out-of-range or negative id there just fails the call (returns false, or nil for the getters). The toggle functions and ShroudSetButtonTransition do NOT: they only check the id against the upper bound, so a negative id indexes the backing list with a negative index and throws (surfacing as a Lua error). Pass ids you actually got back from a create call. The ButtonMode, Transition, and ContentType enums are exposed as Lua globals, so pass members like ButtonMode.Normal, Transition.ColorTint, or ContentType.Password. Colors are Unity HTML hex strings and must include the leading #.

Function Call What it does
ShroudSetButtonColor ShroudSetButtonColor(id, mode, hexColor) Sets one state color of a button
ShroudSetButtonImage ShroudSetButtonImage(id, mode, textureID) Sets one state sprite of a button
ShroudSetButtonTransition ShroudSetButtonTransition(id, transition) Chooses how a button shows state
ShroudGetInputText ShroudGetInputText(id) Reads an input field's full text
ShroudSetInputText ShroudSetInputText(id, text) Sets an input field's text
ShroudSetInputContentType ShroudSetInputContentType(id, type) Sets input validation/keyboard type
ShroudSetPlaceholderText ShroudSetPlaceholderText(id, text) Sets an input's empty-state hint text
ShroudSetInputBackgroundColor ShroudSetInputBackgroundColor(id, hexColor) Tints an input field's background
ShroudSetInputCharacterLimit ShroudSetInputCharacterLimit(id, limit) Caps how many characters fit
ShroudSetInputReadonly ShroudSetInputReadonly(id, isOn) Locks an input against typing
ShroudGetToggle ShroudGetToggle(id) Reads a toggle's checked state
ShroudSetToggle ShroudSetToggle(id, enabled) Sets a toggle's checked state
ShroudSetToggleReadonly ShroudSetToggleReadonly(id, enabled) Sets whether a toggle is interactable

ShroudSetButtonColor¶

ShroudSetButtonColor(id: number, mode: ButtonMode, hexColor: string) -> boolean

  • id: number. The 0-based button id from ShroudUIButton.
  • mode: ButtonMode. Which state to color. Valid: ButtonMode.Normal, ButtonMode.Highlighted, ButtonMode.Pressed, ButtonMode.Disabled. ButtonMode.None is rejected.
  • hexColor: string. Unity HTML hex color, include the leading # (for example #3366CCFF).
  • Returns: boolean. false if mode is ButtonMode.None, or id is negative or out of range; otherwise true.
  • Notes: there is no parse-failure return. The hex string is parsed with ColorUtility.TryParseHtmlString, but its success flag is ignored, so an unparseable string (or a bare hex value missing the leading #) does not fail the call. Instead the color is left at the default fully-transparent black (0,0,0,0), which is still applied and the call still returns true (for a valid id). Always pass a valid #-prefixed hex string and check it yourself. Each call also assigns a brand-new color block that carries only the one state you set, so the other three state colors (and the fade duration and color multiplier) reset to zero. Set every state you care about in the same pass, and expect the colors to show only when the button's transition is Transition.ColorTint.
local btn = ShroudUIButton(0, 0, 120, 30, 0, 0, UI.None, -1)
ShroudSetButtonTransition(btn, Transition.ColorTint)
ShroudSetButtonColor(btn, ButtonMode.Normal, "#2E7D32FF")
ShroudSetButtonColor(btn, ButtonMode.Highlighted, "#43A047FF")
ShroudSetButtonColor(btn, ButtonMode.Pressed, "#1B5E20FF")
ShroudSetButtonColor(btn, ButtonMode.Disabled, "#555555FF")

ShroudSetButtonImage¶

ShroudSetButtonImage(id: number, mode: ButtonMode, textureID: number) -> boolean

  • id: number. The 0-based button id from ShroudUIButton.
  • mode: ButtonMode. Which state's sprite to set. Valid: ButtonMode.Normal, ButtonMode.Highlighted, ButtonMode.Pressed, ButtonMode.Disabled. ButtonMode.None is rejected.
  • textureID: number. A texture id previously returned by ShroudLoadTexture; must be 0 or greater and currently loaded.
  • Returns: boolean. false if mode is ButtonMode.None, id or textureID is negative, or the texture id is not loaded; otherwise true.
  • Notes: ButtonMode.Normal replaces the button's base Image sprite directly. Highlighted, Pressed, and Disabled go into the button's sprite state and only appear when the transition is Transition.SpriteSwap.
local tex = ShroudLoadTexture("button_idle.png")
local btn = ShroudUIButton(0, 40, 120, 30, 0, 0, UI.None, -1)
ShroudSetButtonTransition(btn, Transition.SpriteSwap)
if ShroudSetButtonImage(btn, ButtonMode.Normal, tex) then
    ShroudConsoleLog("button sprite set")
end

ShroudSetButtonTransition¶

ShroudSetButtonTransition(id: number, transition: Transition) -> boolean

  • id: number. The 0-based button id from ShroudUIButton.
  • transition: Transition. How the button reflects its state. Valid: Transition.None, Transition.ColorTint, Transition.SpriteSwap.
  • Returns: boolean. Returns true whenever the id is in range, and also falls through to true when transition is not one of the three valid values, so the return value is not a reliable success check.
  • Notes: the id is only bounds-checked against the upper end (id < count) with no >= 0 guard, so a negative id indexes the button list with a negative index and throws (a Lua error), not a false return. Pass an id you got back from ShroudUIButton. Pick Transition.ColorTint before setting state colors with ShroudSetButtonColor, or Transition.SpriteSwap before setting state sprites with ShroudSetButtonImage.
local btn = ShroudUIButton(0, 80, 120, 30, 0, 0, UI.None, -1)
ShroudSetButtonTransition(btn, Transition.ColorTint)
ShroudSetButtonColor(btn, ButtonMode.Highlighted, "#FFD54FFF")

ShroudGetInputText¶

ShroudGetInputText(id: number) -> string

  • id: number. The 0-based input id from ShroudUIInput.
  • Returns: string, the full field contents. Returns nil if id is negative or out of range.
  • Notes: returns the complete value, not just the portion currently scrolled into view.
local field = ShroudUIInput(0, 0, 200, 24, -1, UI.None)
local typed = ShroudGetInputText(field)
if typed ~= nil then
    ShroudConsoleLog("player entered: " .. typed)
end

ShroudSetInputText¶

ShroudSetInputText(id: number, text: string) -> boolean

  • id: number. The 0-based input id from ShroudUIInput.
  • text: string. The value to place in the field. Defaults to an empty string, so calling with no text clears it.
  • Returns: boolean. false if id is negative or out of range; otherwise true.
local field = ShroudUIInput(0, 0, 200, 24, -1, UI.None)
ShroudSetInputText(field, "Britannia")

ShroudSetInputContentType¶

ShroudSetInputContentType(id: number, type: ContentType) -> boolean

  • id: number. The 0-based input id from ShroudUIInput.
  • type: ContentType. The validation and keyboard mode. Valid: ContentType.Standard, ContentType.Autocorrected, ContentType.IntegerNumber, ContentType.DecimalNumber, ContentType.Alphanumeric, ContentType.Name, ContentType.EmailAddress, ContentType.Password, ContentType.Pin, ContentType.Custom. Defaults to ContentType.Standard.
  • Returns: boolean. false if id is negative or out of range; otherwise true.
local pwd = ShroudUIInput(0, 30, 200, 24, -1, UI.None)
ShroudSetInputContentType(pwd, ContentType.Password)

ShroudSetPlaceholderText¶

ShroudSetPlaceholderText(id: number, text: string) -> boolean

  • id: number. The 0-based input id from ShroudUIInput.
  • text: string. The greyed-out hint shown while the field is empty. Defaults to an empty string.
  • Returns: boolean. false if id is negative or out of range; otherwise true.
local field = ShroudUIInput(0, 60, 200, 24, -1, UI.None)
ShroudSetPlaceholderText(field, "Enter your name")

ShroudSetInputBackgroundColor¶

ShroudSetInputBackgroundColor(id: number, hexColor: string) -> boolean

  • id: number. The 0-based input id from ShroudUIInput.
  • hexColor: string. Unity HTML hex color for the field's background graphic. Include the leading # (for example #202020FF).
  • Returns: boolean. false if id is negative or out of range; otherwise true.
  • Notes: the hex string is parsed before the # is applied, so a bare hex value without # fails to parse and leaves the color black. Always pass the leading #.
local field = ShroudUIInput(0, 90, 200, 24, -1, UI.None)
ShroudSetInputBackgroundColor(field, "#1A1A1AFF")

ShroudSetInputCharacterLimit¶

ShroudSetInputCharacterLimit(id: number, limit: number) -> boolean

  • id: number. The 0-based input id from ShroudUIInput.
  • limit: number. Maximum characters the field accepts. Use 0 for no limit.
  • Returns: boolean. false if id is negative or out of range; otherwise true.
local field = ShroudUIInput(0, 120, 200, 24, -1, UI.None)
ShroudSetInputCharacterLimit(field, 16)

ShroudSetInputReadonly¶

ShroudSetInputReadonly(id: number, isOn: boolean) -> boolean

  • id: number. The 0-based input id from ShroudUIInput.
  • isOn: boolean. true makes the field read-only (no typing), false re-enables editing.
  • Returns: boolean. false if id is negative or out of range; otherwise true.
local field = ShroudUIInput(0, 150, 200, 24, -1, UI.None)
ShroudSetInputText(field, "read-only value")
ShroudSetInputReadonly(field, true)

ShroudGetToggle¶

ShroudGetToggle(id: number) -> boolean

  • id: number. The 0-based toggle id from ShroudUIToggle.
  • Returns: boolean, the toggle's checked state (true = checked). Returns nil if id is at or past the top of the range.
  • Notes: only the upper bound is checked (id < count); there is no >= 0 guard, so a negative id indexes the toggle list with a negative index and throws (a Lua error) rather than returning nil. Only pass ids you got back from ShroudUIToggle.
local box = ShroudUIToggle(0, 0, 20, 20, -1, UI.None)
if ShroudGetToggle(box) == true then
    ShroudConsoleLog("option is on")
end

ShroudSetToggle¶

ShroudSetToggle(id: number, enabled: boolean) -> boolean

  • id: number. The 0-based toggle id from ShroudUIToggle.
  • enabled: boolean. true checks the toggle, false unchecks it.
  • Returns: boolean. false if id is at or past the top of the range; otherwise true.
  • Notes: only the upper bound is checked (id < count); there is no >= 0 guard, so a negative id indexes the toggle list with a negative index and throws (a Lua error) rather than returning false. Only pass ids you got back from ShroudUIToggle.
local box = ShroudUIToggle(0, 0, 20, 20, -1, UI.None)
ShroudSetToggle(box, true)

ShroudSetToggleReadonly¶

ShroudSetToggleReadonly(id: number, enabled: boolean) -> boolean

  • id: number. The 0-based toggle id from ShroudUIToggle.
  • enabled: boolean. Sets the toggle's interactable flag. The argument is interactability, not read-only-ness: pass true to let the player click it, false to lock it. Despite the name, ShroudSetToggleReadonly(id, true) makes the toggle interactive, and false makes it read-only.
  • Returns: boolean. false if id is at or past the top of the range; otherwise true.
  • Notes: only the upper bound is checked (id < count); there is no >= 0 guard, so a negative id indexes the toggle list with a negative index and throws (a Lua error) rather than returning false. Only pass ids you got back from ShroudUIToggle.
local box = ShroudUIToggle(0, 0, 20, 20, -1, UI.None)
ShroudSetToggle(box, true)
ShroudSetToggleReadonly(box, false) -- lock it so the player cannot change it

Legacy immediate-mode drawing¶

These functions wrap Unity's IMGUI (GUI.*) and are being phased out in favor of the retained-mode ShroudUI* widgets. They only draw when called from inside your ShroudOnGUI() callback; called anywhere else they do nothing useful. They are immediate-mode, so you must re-issue every call every frame — nothing persists. All coordinates are screen pixels with the origin at the top-left. GOTCHA: despite the lrx/lry parameter names, ShroudGUILabel and ShroudDrawTexture pass those last two values to a Unity Rect as width and height, not as a lower-right corner. ShroudButton, ShroudButtonRepeat, and ShroudDrawTexture require a valid textureID from ShroudLoadTexture and return false (drawing nothing) if the id does not resolve.

Hover tooltips (ShroudGUITooltip, ShroudDrawTextureTooltip, API v3) register a hover region for the current ShroudOnGUI pass; after every addon has drawn, the host renders the topmost hovered region's text in a styled box near the cursor (so an icon's tooltip always draws above the icons it overlaps). See Buff Icons for a worked example that labels each buff icon with its skill name.

Function Call What it does
ShroudGUILabel ShroudGUILabel(ulx, uly, width, height, text) Draws a text label in a rect
ShroudButton ShroudButton(x, y, width, height, textureID, text, tooltip) Draws a clickable button
ShroudButtonRepeat ShroudButtonRepeat(x, y, width, height, textureID, text, tooltip) Draws a button that fires while held
ShroudDrawTexture ShroudDrawTexture(ulx, uly, width, height, textureID) Draws a loaded texture in a rect
ShroudDrawTextureTooltip ShroudDrawTextureTooltip(ulx, uly, width, height, textureID, text) Draws a texture that shows text on hover
ShroudGUITooltip ShroudGUITooltip(ulx, uly, width, height, text) Registers a hover region with tooltip text

ShroudGUILabel¶

ShroudGUILabel(ulx: number, uly: number, width: number, height: number, text: string) -> boolean

  • ulx: number. Left edge of the label rect, in screen pixels from the left.
  • uly: number. Top edge of the label rect, in screen pixels from the top.
  • width: number. Rect width in pixels. Named lrx/lower-right in older code, but it is used as width.
  • height: number. Rect height in pixels. Named lry/lower-right in older code, but it is used as height.
  • text: string. The text to draw, using the default IMGUI label style.
  • Returns: boolean. Always true; there is no failure sentinel.
  • Notes: Call only from ShroudOnGUI(); it draws for a single frame, so re-issue it every frame. Marked obsolete in the client and slated for removal.
function ShroudOnGUI()
    local fps = math.floor(1 / ShroudDeltaTime)
    ShroudGUILabel(20, 20, 200, 24, "FPS: " .. fps)
end

ShroudButton¶

ShroudButton(x: number, y: number, width: number, height: number, textureID: number, text: string, tooltip: string) -> boolean

  • x: number. Left edge of the button rect, in screen pixels.
  • y: number. Top edge of the button rect, in screen pixels.
  • width: number. Button width in pixels.
  • height: number. Button height in pixels.
  • textureID: number. Texture id from ShroudLoadTexture, drawn as the button image. Required; a bad id makes the call return false and draw nothing.
  • text: string. Caption drawn on the button. Pass "" for none.
  • tooltip: string. IMGUI tooltip text. Pass "" for none.
  • Returns: boolean. true on the frame the button is clicked, otherwise false. Also false if textureID does not resolve, so a click and a missing texture are indistinguishable from the return value alone.
  • Notes: Call only from ShroudOnGUI(). Because a valid texture is required, load one even for a mostly-text button.
local btnTex = -1

function ShroudOnStart()
    btnTex = ShroudLoadTexture("button_bg.png")
end

function ShroudOnGUI()
    if ShroudButton(40, 60, 120, 30, btnTex, "Wave", "Play the wave emote") then
        ShroudPlayEmote("wave")
    end
end

ShroudButtonRepeat¶

ShroudButtonRepeat(x: number, y: number, width: number, height: number, textureID: number, text: string, tooltip: string) -> boolean

Same as ShroudButton but it returns true on every frame the button is held down, not only on the initial click. Same parameters, same failure sentinel (false when textureID does not resolve), and the same ShroudOnGUI()-only requirement. Use it for hold-to-repeat actions and throttle in your own code, since it can fire many times per second.

function ShroudOnGUI()
    if ShroudButtonRepeat(40, 100, 120, 30, btnTex, "Scroll", "Hold to scroll") then
        offset = offset + 1
    end
end

ShroudDrawTexture¶

ShroudDrawTexture(ulx: number, uly: number, width: number, height: number, textureID: number) -> boolean

  • ulx: number. Left edge of the draw rect, in screen pixels.
  • uly: number. Top edge of the draw rect, in screen pixels.
  • width: number. Rect width in pixels. Named lrx/lower-right in older code but used as width; the texture is stretched to fill it.
  • height: number. Rect height in pixels. Named as a lower-right coordinate but used as height.
  • textureID: number. Texture id from ShroudLoadTexture.
  • Returns: boolean. true on success, false if textureID does not resolve to a loaded texture.
  • Notes: Call only from ShroudOnGUI(). The texture is scaled to the rect; query its native size with ShroudGetTextureSize if you need to preserve aspect ratio.
local logo = -1

function ShroudOnStart()
    logo = ShroudLoadTexture("logo.png")
end

function ShroudOnGUI()
    if not ShroudDrawTexture(300, 20, 128, 64, logo) then
        ShroudConsoleLog("logo texture failed to load")
    end
end

ShroudDrawTextureTooltip¶

ShroudDrawTextureTooltip(ulx: number, uly: number, width: number, height: number, textureID: number, text: string) -> boolean (API v3)

  • ulx, uly, width, height, textureID: same as ShroudDrawTexture.
  • text: string. Tooltip shown while the cursor is over this rect. An empty/nil string draws the texture with no tooltip.
  • Returns: boolean. true on success, false if textureID does not resolve (the tooltip region is still registered).
  • Notes: Call only from ShroudOnGUI(). Draws the texture and registers its hover region in one call. The host renders the tooltip after every addon's ShroudOnGUI, so it always sits above the icons. When rects overlap, the last one drawn under the cursor wins.
function ShroudOnGUI()
    local tex = ShroudGetBuffIcon(0)
    if tex >= 0 then
        ShroudDrawTextureTooltip(40, 220, 40, 40, tex, ShroudGetBuffTooltip(0))
    end
end

ShroudGUITooltip¶

ShroudGUITooltip(ulx: number, uly: number, width: number, height: number, text: string) -> boolean (API v3)

  • ulx, uly, width, height: the hover rect, same convention as ShroudDrawTexture.
  • text: string. Tooltip shown while the cursor is over the rect.
  • Returns: boolean. Always true.
  • Notes: Call only from ShroudOnGUI(). Registers a hover region without drawing anything, so you can attach a tooltip to something you drew yourself (a ShroudGUILabel, a widget, an empty area). Registration lasts one GUI pass; re-issue it every frame.
function ShroudOnGUI()
    ShroudGUILabel(40, 200, 200, 24, "Focus: " .. ShroudGetStatValueByName("Focus"))
    ShroudGUITooltip(40, 200, 200, 24, "Your current focus pool")
end

Textures and sound¶

These functions load and manage addon-supplied textures (PNG/JPG under the addon's Lua folder) and audio clips, and control playback of sounds, the scene music stack, and game effects. Two traps run through the group: every path is confined to the addon folder, so a path that escapes it (via ..) fails with -1 (textures) or false (sound); and the sound system mixes number bases. Sound clip ids passed to ShroudPlaySound are 1-based, ShroudStopSound/ShroudIsChannelPlaying take a 1-based channel, but ShroudPlaySound returns a 0-based channel index, so you must add 1 before feeding it back to a stop/query call. ShroudLoadSound also loads asynchronously: it returns immediately and the clip only appears in ShroudListSound() once the load finishes.

Function Call What it does
ShroudLoadTexture ShroudLoadTexture(path) Load an image file as a texture handle
ShroudSetTextureClamp ShroudSetTextureClamp(id, clamp) Set a texture's wrap mode clamp/repeat
ShroudGetTextureSize ShroudGetTextureSize(id) Return a texture's pixel width and height
ShroudLoadSound ShroudLoadSound(path, audioType) Start async load of an audio clip
ShroudListSound ShroudListSound() List names of loaded sound clips
ShroudListSoundReset ShroudListSoundReset() Stop all channels and clear loaded clips
ShroudPlaySound ShroudPlaySound(id, volume) Play a loaded clip, returns its channel
ShroudStopSound ShroudStopSound(channel) Stop a playing channel
ShroudIsChannelPlaying ShroudIsChannelPlaying(channel) Name of the clip on a channel
ShroudStopUISound ShroudStopUISound() Stop the game's current UI sound
ShroudSceneMusic ShroudSceneMusic(active) Resume or stop the scene music stack
ShroudStopFX ShroudStopFX(fxName) Stop a tracked game effect by name

ShroudLoadTexture¶

ShroudLoadTexture(path: string) -> number

  • path (string): file path relative to the addon's Lua folder (for example "images/icon.png"). PNG and JPG are decoded by Texture2D.LoadImage.
  • Returns a texture handle (number, starting at 1) used by the texture, image, and draw functions. Returns -1 if the file does not exist, fails to decode, or the path escapes the addon folder.
  • Notes: loading the same file path twice returns the same handle (results are cached by path, case-insensitive). The default wrap mode is Repeat; use ShroudSetTextureClamp to switch it to Clamp.
local tex = ShroudLoadTexture("images/banner.png")
if tex == -1 then
    ShroudConsoleLog("banner.png failed to load")
else
    -- draw it into an image widget created elsewhere
    ShroudModifyImage(imageId, UI.Image, tex)
end

ShroudSetTextureClamp¶

ShroudSetTextureClamp(id: number, clamp: boolean) -> boolean

  • id (number): a texture handle from ShroudLoadTexture.
  • clamp (boolean): true sets wrap mode Clamp (edge pixels stretch, no tiling); false sets Repeat (tiling).
  • Returns true on success, false if the handle is unknown.
local tex = ShroudLoadTexture("images/frame.png")
ShroudSetTextureClamp(tex, true)

ShroudGetTextureSize¶

ShroudGetTextureSize(id: number) -> number, number

  • id (number): a texture handle from ShroudLoadTexture.
  • Returns two numbers, the texture's pixel width and height, as a multi-value tuple. Returns nil (a single value) if the handle is unknown, so guard the first return before use.
local tex = ShroudLoadTexture("images/map.png")
local w, h = ShroudGetTextureSize(tex)
if w ~= nil then
    ShroudConsoleLog("map is " .. w .. "x" .. h)
end

ShroudLoadSound¶

ShroudLoadSound(path: string, audioType: AudioType.OGGVORBIS) -> boolean

  • path (string): file path relative to the addon's Lua folder.
  • audioType (enum): the clip's real format, from the exposed AudioType enum. Useful members: AudioType.WAV, AudioType.OGGVORBIS, AudioType.MPEG. It must match the file's actual encoding.
  • Returns true if the load request was accepted (path exists inside the addon folder), false if the path escapes the folder. true does NOT mean the clip is ready.
  • Notes: the load runs asynchronously on a coroutine. The clip is appended to the sound list only when the web request completes, so its playable id (its 1-based position in that list) is assigned by load-completion order. Poll ShroudListSound to find loaded clips before calling ShroudPlaySound. Decode errors are logged, not returned.
ShroudLoadSound("sounds/chime.ogg", AudioType.OGGVORBIS)
-- later, once the load has finished:
for i, name in ipairs(ShroudListSound()) do
    ShroudConsoleLog("clip " .. i .. " = " .. name)
end

ShroudListSound¶

ShroudListSound() -> list

  • Returns a list (table) of the names of every loaded sound clip, in load order. The 1-based index into this list is the id you pass to ShroudPlaySound. Returns an empty list when nothing is loaded.
local clips = ShroudListSound()
if #clips > 0 then
    ShroudPlaySound(1, 80)  -- play the first loaded clip at 80% volume
end

ShroudListSoundReset¶

ShroudListSoundReset() -> boolean

  • Stops every playback channel and clears the loaded-clip list, invalidating all clip ids. Returns true if any clips were loaded (and were cleared), false if the list was already empty.
  • Notes: after a reset, clip ids restart from 1 as new clips load.
if ShroudListSoundReset() then
    ShroudConsoleLog("sound cache cleared")
end

ShroudPlaySound¶

ShroudPlaySound(id: number, volume: number) -> number

  • id (number): 1-based clip id, its position in ShroudListSound. Values of 0 or greater than the loaded count are rejected.
  • volume (number): playback volume 0 to 100 (converted internally to 0.0 to 1.0).
  • Returns the 0-based channel index (0 to 4) the clip started on. Returns -1 if the id is invalid or all five channels are already busy.
  • Notes: there are five playback channels. The returned index is 0-based, but ShroudStopSound and ShroudIsChannelPlaying take a 1-based channel, so add 1 before passing it back. Playing a sound also fires the addon's ShroudOnPlaySound callback with the clip name.
local ch = ShroudPlaySound(1, 75)
if ch >= 0 then
    -- convert the 0-based return to the 1-based channel the stop/query calls expect
    local channel = ch + 1
    ShroudConsoleLog("playing on channel " .. channel)
end

ShroudStopSound¶

ShroudStopSound(channel: number) -> boolean

  • channel (number): 1-based channel number, 1 to 5. Remember ShroudPlaySound returns a 0-based index, so add 1.
  • Returns true if that channel was playing and was stopped, false if the channel number is out of range or nothing was playing on it.
local ch = ShroudPlaySound(2, 60)
if ch >= 0 then
    ShroudStopSound(ch + 1)  -- stop it immediately
end

ShroudIsChannelPlaying¶

ShroudIsChannelPlaying(channel: number) -> string

  • channel (number): 1-based channel number, 1 to 5.
  • Returns the name of the clip currently playing on that channel, or an empty string "" if the channel is out of range or idle.
local name = ShroudIsChannelPlaying(1)
if name ~= "" then
    ShroudConsoleLog("channel 1 is playing " .. name)
end

ShroudStopUISound¶

ShroudStopUISound() -> boolean

  • Stops the game's currently playing UI sound effect (through the game audio manager), not addon-loaded clips. Returns true if the audio manager was available, false otherwise.
ShroudStopUISound()

ShroudSceneMusic¶

ShroudSceneMusic(active: boolean) -> boolean

  • active (boolean): true resumes the scene's default music stack; false stops the music stack.
  • Returns true in both cases. This drives the game's music, independent of addon-loaded sounds.
-- mute scene music while your addon plays its own audio
ShroudSceneMusic(false)
ShroudPlaySound(1, 100)

ShroudStopFX¶

ShroudStopFX(fxName: string) -> boolean

  • fxName (string): the GameObject name of a game effect the addon is tracking. The addon only tracks effects it was notified of through the ShroudOnPlayFX callback.
  • Returns true if a tracked effect with that name was found and ended, false if no such effect is tracked.
  • Notes: the call also prunes destroyed effects from the tracked list as a side effect.
-- ShroudOnPlayFX(name, isOn) records fxName when the game starts an effect
function ShroudOnPlayFX(name, isOn)
    if isOn and name == "Fx_Torch" then
        ShroudStopFX(name)  -- suppress that effect
    end
end

Console, garbage collection, and timers¶

Output, memory, and timer utilities. ShroudConsoleLog and the overridden print write to the in-game Lua chat console; ShroudUseLuaConsoleForPrint chooses whether print goes there or to the player-invisible engine log. The collectgarbage built-in is replaced with a client-safe version (#914) so an addon cannot stall or disable the shared GC. Timers are named: ShroudRegisterPeriodic calls a named global function on an interval, and the throttle is a 0.01s minimum period. These functions are valid at any time (they do not require a callback context), but the settings they change (print routing, the periodic list) are process-wide and shared by every loaded addon.

Function Call What it does
ShroudConsoleLog ShroudConsoleLog(message) Write a line to the Lua chat console
ShroudUseLuaConsoleForPrint ShroudUseLuaConsoleForPrint(useConsole) Route print to chat or to the engine log
print print(...) Overridden: prints to the Lua chat console
collectgarbage collectgarbage(mode, arg) Overridden: measure or step the managed GC
ShroudForceGC ShroudForceGC() Run a full blocking garbage collect
ShroudRegisterPeriodic ShroudRegisterPeriodic(name, functionName, period, repeating) Call a named function on a timer
ShroudRemovePeriodic ShroudRemovePeriodic(name) Cancel a named timer
ShroudListPeriodics ShroudListPeriodics() List the names of active timers

ShroudConsoleLog¶

ShroudConsoleLog(message: string) -> string

  • message (string): the text to print. [url... markup is defused to [... before display.
  • Returns (string): the message actually logged (with the [url substitution applied). Returns nil if message was nil.
  • Notes: writes a chat entry of type LuaMessage with ForceVisible = false, so it appears in the chat log but does not force the chat window open. The un-prefixed alias ConsoleLog is registered to the same function.
local scene = ShroudGetCurrentSceneName()
ShroudConsoleLog("Addon loaded in scene: " .. scene)

ShroudUseLuaConsoleForPrint¶

ShroudUseLuaConsoleForPrint(useConsole: boolean) -> boolean

  • useConsole (boolean): true routes print output to the in-game Lua chat console (via ShroudConsoleLog); false routes it to the engine's Console.WriteLine, which players do not see.
  • Returns (boolean): always true.
  • Notes: this sets Script.DefaultOptions.DebugPrint, which is process-wide, so it changes print routing for every loaded addon, not just yours. The default at startup is the chat console (true).
-- Send print output to the engine log instead of player chat while debugging.
ShroudUseLuaConsoleForPrint(false)
print("this goes to the engine log, not chat")
ShroudUseLuaConsoleForPrint(true)

print¶

print(...) -> nil

  • ... (any): one or more values, converted to strings and joined with tabs, exactly like standard Lua print.
  • Returns (nil).
  • Notes: this host overrides the stock print. Output is routed through Script.DefaultOptions.DebugPrint, which by default is the Lua chat console, so print writes to in-game chat like ShroudConsoleLog. ShroudUseLuaConsoleForPrint(false) redirects it to the player-invisible engine log; ShroudUseLuaConsoleForPrint(true) restores chat output. The routing is shared by all addons.
local hp = ShroudPlayerCurrentHealth
print("Health is", hp)  -- appears in the Lua chat console

collectgarbage¶

collectgarbage(mode: string, arg: number) -> number | boolean | (number, number) | nil

  • mode (string, optional): one of "collect", "restart", "count", "step", "isrunning", or any other Lua 5.2 mode name. Absent is treated as "collect".
  • arg (number, optional): only used with "step", where it is a millisecond time budget for the incremental collect (default 3, clamped to the 0.1–50 range). Note this is a time budget, not Lua's KB step size.
  • Returns: depends on mode — "collect"/"restart"/absent run a full blocking collect and return the number 0; "count" returns two numbers (managedKB, bytesMod1024) from the managed heap; "step" returns a boolean that is true when the collection cycle is complete; "isrunning" returns a boolean; any other mode ("stop", "setpause", "setstepmul", ...) returns nil.
  • Notes: this replaces MoonSharp's stock collectgarbage (#914). Modes that would let an addon disable the GC shared by the whole client are intentionally no-ops returning nil. "step" never falls back to a blocking collect; when incremental GC is unavailable it self-guards and reports complete. Prefer "step" over the blocking "collect" to avoid a 140–190ms stall.
local kb = collectgarbage("count")           -- managed heap size in KB
ShroudConsoleLog(string.format("Lua heap: %.0f KB", kb))
local done = collectgarbage("step", 2)        -- 2ms incremental slice
if not done then ShroudConsoleLog("GC has more work to do") end

ShroudForceGC¶

ShroudForceGC() -> boolean

  • Returns (boolean): always true.
  • Notes: runs a full, blocking Gen2 GC.Collect(), which can stall the client for roughly 140–190ms. Prefer collectgarbage("step") for incremental collection; use this only when a hard, immediate collect is genuinely needed.
ShroudForceGC()
ShroudConsoleLog("Heap after forced GC: " .. tostring(collectgarbage("count")) .. " KB")

ShroudRegisterPeriodic¶

ShroudRegisterPeriodic(name: string, functionName: string, period: number, repeating: boolean) -> boolean

  • name (string): an identifier for this timer, used later with ShroudRemovePeriodic and shown by ShroudListPeriodics. Registering a name that already exists removes the previous timer with that name first.
  • functionName (string): the name of a global function to call. It is looked up in the script globals at registration time; the function is invoked with no arguments.
  • period (number): seconds between calls. Must be at least 0.01; a smaller value registers nothing and returns false.
  • repeating (boolean): true fires every period seconds; false fires once and then removes itself.
  • Returns (boolean): true on success, false if period is below 0.01 or functionName does not resolve to an existing global value.
  • Notes: the target is resolved by name, so define the function as a global before calling this. The callback takes no parameters — read whatever state it needs from the API directly.
function TickHealth()
    ShroudConsoleLog("HP: " .. ShroudPlayerCurrentHealth)
end
-- Call TickHealth every 5 seconds under the name "hpwatch".
ShroudRegisterPeriodic("hpwatch", "TickHealth", 5.0, true)

ShroudRemovePeriodic¶

ShroudRemovePeriodic(name: string) -> boolean

  • name (string): the timer identifier passed to ShroudRegisterPeriodic.
  • Returns (boolean): true if a timer with that name was found and removed, false if no such timer exists.
if ShroudRemovePeriodic("hpwatch") then
    ShroudConsoleLog("Stopped the hpwatch timer")
end

ShroudListPeriodics¶

ShroudListPeriodics() -> list

  • Returns (list): the names of all currently registered timers. Empty when none are active.
  • Notes: the value is a MoonSharp enumerator over the names, so drive it with a generic for as shown. Names appear in scheduled-time order.
for name in ShroudListPeriodics() do
    ShroudConsoleLog("Active timer: " .. name)
end

Ink conversation bridge¶

These four functions read and write the same per-character variable store that player-authored custom-NPC Ink scripts use through their saveVariable/loadVariable external functions, letting an addon and a conversation share state. Each value lives in a PlayerPrefs key formed as <characterName>.Ink_<varName>, so varName must be a non-empty Lua string (no numeric coercion) and a character must be logged in — otherwise the load/has/delete calls return nil or false and a save returns false. Values are stored as strings: integral numbers are written without a decimal point ("42"), booleans map to "1"/"0", and the read side always hands back a string. Writes are not flushed immediately (they persist on a clean client quit), and a running conversation only observes an addon's write at its next loadVariable.

Function Call What it does
ShroudLoadInkVariable ShroudLoadInkVariable(varName) Read a stored Ink variable as a string
ShroudSaveInkVariable ShroudSaveInkVariable(varName, value) Store a string, number, or boolean
ShroudHasInkVariable ShroudHasInkVariable(varName) Test whether a value is stored
ShroudDeleteInkVariable ShroudDeleteInkVariable(varName) Remove a stored value

ShroudLoadInkVariable¶

ShroudLoadInkVariable(varName: string) -> string | nil

  • varName (string): variable name, shared with the Ink side. Must be a non-empty string; a number or other type is rejected.
  • Returns: the stored value as a string, or nil when no value is stored, when varName is not a non-empty string, or when no character is logged in.
  • Notes: existence is exact — a value that was saved as an empty string, or the literal "null" the Ink side treats as its own unsaved sentinel, still comes back as a string, not nil.
local greeted = ShroudLoadInkVariable("met_the_smith")
if greeted == "1" then
    ShroudConsoleLog("Player already met the smith")
else
    ShroudConsoleLog("First visit to the smith")
end

ShroudSaveInkVariable¶

ShroudSaveInkVariable(varName: string, value: string | number | boolean) -> boolean

  • varName (string): variable name to write. Must be a non-empty string.
  • value (string, number, or boolean): the value to store. A string is capped at 8192 characters; an integral number in the range +/-9.2e18 is written with no decimal point so the Ink side parses it back as an int; a boolean stores as "1" or "0".
  • Returns: boolean. true on success; false when varName is not a non-empty string, when no character is logged in, when the value type is not string/number/boolean, when a string exceeds 8192 characters, or when a number is NaN or infinite.
  • Notes: the write is not flushed to disk immediately (parity with the Ink side, and to avoid main-thread I/O from an addon writing every frame); Unity persists it on a clean quit. A conversation in progress sees the new value only at its next loadVariable.
local ok = ShroudSaveInkVariable("reputation", 42)
if ok then
    ShroudConsoleLog("Reputation stored for this conversation")
else
    ShroudConsoleLog("Save failed (logged out or bad value)")
end

ShroudHasInkVariable¶

ShroudHasInkVariable(varName: string) -> boolean

  • varName (string): variable name to test. Must be a non-empty string.
  • Returns: boolean. true only when a value is stored for this character under varName; false when nothing is stored, when varName is not a non-empty string, or when no character is logged in.
if not ShroudHasInkVariable("quest_started") then
    ShroudSaveInkVariable("quest_started", true)
    ShroudConsoleLog("Marked quest as started")
end

ShroudDeleteInkVariable¶

ShroudDeleteInkVariable(varName: string) -> boolean

  • varName (string): variable name to remove. Must be a non-empty string.
  • Returns: boolean. true when a stored value existed and was removed; false when nothing was stored, when varName is not a non-empty string, or when no character is logged in.
if ShroudDeleteInkVariable("temp_flag") then
    ShroudConsoleLog("Cleared temp_flag")
else
    ShroudConsoleLog("Nothing to clear")
end

Saved variables¶

Per-addon persistent storage. Each value is written into a JSON file inside the addon sandbox at Lua/SavedVariables/<addon>.<character>.character.json (character scope, one file per character) or Lua/SavedVariables/<addon>.account.json (account scope, shared across characters on this install). The scope argument is an optional string, "character" (the default) or "account"; any other value, including nil, normalizes to "character". Keys are strings up to 128 characters with no control characters and no / or \; an invalid key makes the setters return false and the getter return nil. Writes do not hit disk on every call: ShroudSetSavedVar/ShroudDeleteSavedVar only mark the addon's table dirty, and the dirty tables are flushed at logout, on addon disable/unload, at application quit, and when you call ShroudFlushSavedVars.

Function Call What it does
ShroudSetSavedVar ShroudSetSavedVar(key, value, scope) Store a value under a key
ShroudGetSavedVar ShroudGetSavedVar(key, scope) Read a stored value
ShroudDeleteSavedVar ShroudDeleteSavedVar(key, scope) Remove a stored key
ShroudFlushSavedVars ShroudFlushSavedVars() Write dirty tables to disk now

ShroudSetSavedVar¶

ShroudSetSavedVar(key: string, value: string|number|boolean|table|nil, scope: string) -> boolean

  • key: string. The storage name. Must be non-empty, at most 128 characters, with no control characters and no / or \.
  • value: string, number, boolean, table, or nil. Tables may be nested; they are JSON-serialized on flush. Functions, threads, and userdata are not persistable and cause the call to fail.
  • scope: string, optional. "character" (default) or "account"; matched case-insensitively, anything else falls back to "character".
  • Returns: boolean. true when the value was stored (table marked dirty) — a nil value counts as stored and returns true — false on an invalid key or a non-persistable value type.
  • Notes: does not write to disk. It updates the in-memory table and marks it dirty; the file is written on the next flush trigger (logout, disable/unload, quit, or ShroudFlushSavedVars). Character scope is keyed by the current character, so the same key holds independent values on different characters.
local runs = ShroudGetSavedVar("runCount") or 0
runs = runs + 1
if ShroudSetSavedVar("runCount", runs) then
    ShroudConsoleLog("This addon has now started " .. runs .. " times")
end

-- account-wide preference, visible to all characters
ShroudSetSavedVar("theme", "dark", "account")

ShroudGetSavedVar¶

ShroudGetSavedVar(key: string, scope: string) -> string|number|boolean|table|nil

  • key: string. The storage name to read. Same validity rules as ShroudSetSavedVar.
  • scope: string, optional. "character" (default) or "account"; must match the scope the value was stored under.
  • Returns: the stored value with its original Lua type (string, number, boolean, or table), or nil if the key is unset, the key is invalid, or no saved-variable table exists yet for that addon and scope.
  • Notes: a stored table is returned by reference to the in-memory copy; mutating its fields changes the cached value, but you still must call ShroudSetSavedVar (or otherwise mark the table dirty) for the change to be flagged for the next flush.
local prefs = ShroudGetSavedVar("windowPos")
if prefs then
    ShroudSetSize(panelId, UI.Panel, prefs.w, prefs.h)
else
    ShroudConsoleLog("No saved window position yet")
end

ShroudDeleteSavedVar¶

ShroudDeleteSavedVar(key: string, scope: string) -> boolean

  • key: string. The stored key to remove. Same validity rules as ShroudSetSavedVar.
  • scope: string, optional. "character" (default) or "account".
  • Returns: boolean. true when the key existed and was removed (table marked dirty), false on an invalid key, a missing table, or a key that was not present.
  • Notes: like the setter, this only marks the table dirty; the deletion reaches disk on the next flush.
if ShroudDeleteSavedVar("runCount") then
    ShroudConsoleLog("Cleared the saved run counter")
end

ShroudFlushSavedVars¶

ShroudFlushSavedVars() -> boolean

  • Returns: boolean. true if every dirty addon table was written (also true when nothing was dirty), false if any file failed to write or a table exceeded the 256 KB serialized limit.
  • Notes: forces an immediate write of all pending changes rather than waiting for logout, disable/unload, or quit. A table whose JSON exceeds 256 KB is skipped, not written, and logs a size-limit message to the addon console; the call then returns false.
ShroudSetSavedVar("lastSeen", ShroudGetGameTime().Day, "account")
if not ShroudFlushSavedVars() then
    ShroudConsoleLog("Saved variables did not fully write; check size limits")
end

Data shapes¶

Several API functions return C# objects as Lua userdata with readable fields. Field names and casing below are exactly what Lua sees; read them with dot access (for example info.Name). These are read-only snapshots taken at call time.

RuneEffects¶

Returned as a list by ShroudGetPlayerBuff, ShroudGetPetBuff, and ShroudGetTargetBuff. One entry per active rune/effect group.

Field Type Meaning
RuneName string Display name of the rune/effect.
Effects list List of BuffEffects components under this rune.
RuneId number Rune definition id.
IsDebuff boolean True if the effect is harmful.
StackCount number Count of entries in Effects.
  • StackCount is #Effects, not a true stack count. A rune that applies several effect components counts each one, so treat it as an upper bound.
  • The buff list is a fresh snapshot each call. Call once per frame and reuse it.

BuffEffects¶

Nested inside RuneEffects.Effects; not returned on its own. One entry per effect component of a rune.

Field Type Meaning
Description string Human-readable effect description.
Value number Effect magnitude.
CurrentDuration number Seconds remaining.
TotalDuration number Full duration in seconds.
TotalTick number Number of ticks over the effect's life.

PetInfo¶

Returned by ShroudGetPetInfo; nil when there is no primary pet.

Field Type Meaning
Name string Pet name.
Level number Pet level.
isSummon boolean True if the pet is a summoned creature.
Strength number Strength attribute.
Dexterity number Dexterity attribute.
Intelligence number Intelligence attribute.
CurrentHealth number Current hit points.
MaxHealth number Maximum hit points.
HealthRegen number Out-of-combat health regen.
HealthRegenCombat number In-combat health regen.
AttackSpeed number Attack speed.
Absorb number Physical damage absorbed.
Resist number Physical resistance.
MagicResist number Magic resistance.
TauntPower number Taunt strength.
StrengthPower number Strength-derived power.
CriticalHit number Critical hit chance/power.
MoveSpeed number Movement speed.
MoveRate number Movement rate.
  • Focus fields are not exposed; pets report health only.
  • isSummon is lower-camelCase, unlike the other fields.

GameTime¶

Returned by ShroudGetGameTime.

Field Type Meaning
Day number Day of the month.
Hour number Hour of the in-game day (fractional).
Month number Month of the year.
Year number In-game year.
PeriodOfDay string Named period (for example dawn, day, dusk, night).
Season string Named season.
  • Day and Month are the engine value +1, so they read as 1-based calendar numbers.

SceneCap¶

Returned by ShroudGetSceneCap.

Field Type Meaning
Level number Adventurer/effective level cap for the current scene.
Skill number Skill cap for the current scene.

Deck¶

Returned by ShroudCurrentDeck (single value), and as a list by ShroudDeckList and ShroudGetDeckCardList.

Field Type Meaning
id string Deck or card identifier.
name string Deck or card display name.
quantity number Card count (deck size, or copies of a card).
  • The same shape is reused for whole decks and for individual cards depending on the function that returns it.

LuaVector2¶

Returned by ShroudGetPosition.

Field Type Meaning
x number X coordinate.
y number Y coordinate.

LuaVector3¶

Returned by ShroudWorldToScreenPoint.

Field Type Meaning
x number X coordinate.
y number Y coordinate.
z number Z coordinate (depth for screen-point results). 
local t = ShroudGetGameTime()
if t ~= nil then
    -- Day and Month are 1-based (engine value +1)
    ShroudConsoleLog(string.format("Day %d of month %d, %s (%s)",
        t.Day, t.Month, t.PeriodOfDay, t.Season))
end

Frozen quirks¶

These behaviors are deliberate and load-bearing. Shipped addons already depend on each one, so the client preserves them exactly. Treat them as part of the contract, not as bugs to work around or report.

Quirk What to expect
Mixed index bases: widgets, stats, and buffs are 0-based; sound ids and channels are 1-based Widget handles (UI.Image, UI.Panel, ...), the stat number passed to ShroudGetStatValueByNumber(number: number), and the buff index passed to ShroudGetBuffName(index: number) all start at 0 and run to count - 1. Sound ids passed to ShroudPlaySound(id: number, volume: number) start at 1 (id 0 is rejected and returns -1), and channel arguments to ShroudStopSound(channel: number) / ShroudIsChannelPlaying(channel: number) are also 1-based (channel 0 is rejected). Do not assume one convention across the API; index by domain.
ShroudPlaySound returns a 0-based channel even though channels are otherwise 1-based The return value is the raw audio-source slot, 0-based (first slot returns 0), or -1 on failure (id out of range or no free slot). But ShroudStopSound and ShroudIsChannelPlaying expect a 1-based channel. To stop the sound you just started, add 1 to the value ShroudPlaySound returned.
The ShroudSetDragguable / ShroudUnsetDragguable spelling The drag-enable functions are misspelled with a double g ("Dragguable"). The correct, working names are ShroudSetDragguable(id: number, kind: UI.Image) and ShroudUnsetDragguable(id: number, kind: UI.Image), each returning boolean. A correctly spelled "Draggable" does not exist; call the misspelled names.
ShroudGetGameTime Day and Month are engine value +1 The returned table has Day and Month already incremented by one over the engine's internal 0-based counters, so they read as human 1-based calendar values. Hour, Year, PeriodOfDay, and Season are passed through unchanged. Do not add your own +1. (When game time is unavailable the whole table returns zeros, including Day = 0 / Month = 0.)
ShroudSetParent returns -1 even on success ShroudSetParent(id: number, kind: UI.Image, parentId: number, parentKind: UI.Image): number always returns -1, whether or not the reparent happened. The return value carries no success information. Ignore it and verify the effect visually or by layout, not by the result code.
Un-prefixed aliases for a few calls Five functions are also registered without the Shroud prefix, kept for old addons: ConsoleLog(message: string), GetStatCount(), GetStatValueByNumber(number: number), GetStatNameByNumber(number: number), and GetStatValueByName(name: string). They are exact aliases of their Shroud-prefixed forms. Prefer the prefixed names in new code; the bare names will keep working.
ShroudSwitchDeck is a stub ShroudSwitchDeck(deck: number): boolean does nothing and always returns false. It never changes the active deck. Do not call it expecting a deck swap; there is no Lua path to switch decks.
Stat getters return sentinel values, not nil, for hidden or out-of-range stats For an invisible or out-of-range stat number, the stat getters return -999 (numeric getters) or "INVALID" (name/description getters) instead of nil. The numeric sentinel is exposed as the global InvalidStatResult (= -999). ShroudGetStatCount() reports the full stat enum size, which includes hidden slots, so a plain 0..count-1 loop will hit slots that return these sentinels. Compare against InvalidStatResult / "INVALID" rather than testing for nil.
Buff getters return "Invalid" / -1, not nil, when the index is past the end ShroudGetBuffName(index) and ShroudGetBuffDescription(index) return the string "Invalid" and ShroudGetBuffTimeRemaining(index) returns -1 when index is at or beyond the current buff count. They guard only the upper bound: a negative index is not checked and can error. Read ShroudGetBuffCount() first and iterate 0..count-1.
